# Convex buffer thresholds and the limitation of base-volume transport

This note fixes the body, its mixed measure and covariance, and epsilon>0. It introduces no body variation and proves no Gamma payment. The threshold epigraph is a projection of the existing convex buffered regions with ONE additional scalar coordinate. The exact finite domain and the martingale calibration below are useful distinctions that do not follow from ignoring atomic plateaus.

## 1. Definitions and fixed-body quantiles

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base, let K_p be positive compatible d-dimensional fibers, d>=1, and let C be their canonical convex hull. Write B=conv(P), M=sum_p |K_p|, N=d+1, and let mu be the original mixed measure supported on the sampled fibers. Let Gamma(u) be the fixed positive covariance norm, or any fixed norm on the continuous covectors. All pure-base halfspaces remain closed and receive no buffer.

For a REAL source z in B, y in C_z, and an independent scalar l>=0, put

    f(z,y,l)=[l E_(C_z)(y)/M]^(1/N).

At l=0, or at the boundary of C_z, set f=0, in agreement with continuous extension. Let b_l(z,y) be the infimum of the masses of

    a·(Z-z)+u·(X-y)>=-epsilon Gamma(u) f(z,y,l),

over nonzero continuous u and arbitrary real base covectors a, together with the closed pure-base depth b_base(z). Homogeneity allows ||u||=1 in any fixed Euclidean norm. Fix 0<Q<=M and define

    T_Q(z)=inf{l>=0: some y in C_z has b_l(z,y)>=Q},

with value infinity if there is no such pair, and set T_Q=infinity outside B.

For each a and u!=0 define the right upper quantile

    c_Q(a,u)=max{c:mu[a·Z+u·X>=c]>=Q}.

This maximum is finite. Each positive d-dimensional fiber has a continuous projection distribution for u!=0, so its tail, and their finite sum, are continuous. Thus the mass condition is EXACTLY c<=c_Q(a,u), including Q=M and intervals of zero projected density. No strict-quantile convention is imposed.

## 2. Closed convex epigraph and its exact domain

The previously proved joint concavity of F(z,y)=E_(C_z)(y)^(1/d), followed by weighted geometric-mean concavity, makes

    f=M^(-1/N) F^(d/N) l^(1/N)

jointly concave in (z,y,l) for l>=0. Its extension is continuous on every bounded l slab over C.

The set of feasible triples is therefore the closed convex set given by (z,y) in C, l>=0, b_base(z)>=Q, and ALL inequalities

    a·z+u·y-epsilon Gamma(u) f(z,y,l)<=c_Q(a,u).       (1)

The atomic depth superlevel is closed and convex: it is the intersection of the corresponding closed atomic-quantile halfspaces. Atomic boundary mass is retained here.

Project this set onto (z,l). It is closed, despite the unbounded l coordinate: for a convergent sequence (z_j,l_j), corresponding marks y_j have a subsequence in the fixed compact C. The limit satisfies every inequality (1). Projection also preserves convexity. Increasing l preserves all constraints. Consequently this projection is precisely the epigraph of a nonnegative, lower-semicontinuous extended-valued convex function T_Q. Every finite threshold is ATTAINED by an actual mark.

Its domain is exactly

    dom T_Q={z in B:b_base(z)>=Q}.                       (2)

Necessity is immediate from the unbuffered pure-base competitors. For sufficiency choose any interior mark y in C_z, so E_(C_z)(y)>0. The actual fibers C_z are full dimensional for every z in B by positive sampled fibers and Minkowski inclusion. Choose R with every sampled fiber and y contained in R Ball, and let gamma_min=min_(||u||=1)Gamma(u)>0. Once

    epsilon f(z,y,l) gamma_min>=2R,

every cap in (1) wholly captures every sampled fiber with a·(p-z)>=0. These bases form a closed containing atomic halfspace, of mass at least b_base(z). The pure-base competitors supply the reverse bound. This proves finite feasibility and (2), including equality b_base(z)=Q.

Also T_Q(z)=0 exactly when the ORIGINAL unbuffered depth reaches Q at a mark in C_z. Projection closedness ensures that a sequence of weights tending to zero cannot create an additional zero threshold without such a mark.

Positive-depth feasible marks are interior to C_z. For completeness, at a fiber-boundary mark choose a supporting continuous normal u. The finite support-height roof z↦h_(C_z)(u) is polyhedral and has a finite affine majorant touching at z. The associated ambient supporting plane has nonzero continuous normal, and its captured trace in each sampled fiber has zero d-volume. Hence original depth there is zero; E=0 means buffering does not change it.

## 3. An exact scalar variational formula

For z in dom T_Q and an interior mark y define

    r_Q(z,y)=sup_(a,u!=0)
       [(a·z+u·y-c_Q(a,u))/Gamma(u)]_+.

This is a nonnegative convex function of (z,y), being a supremum of affine positive parts. It is finite on these fibers. Indeed compare the mixed quantile with the atomic quantile for a: bounded continuous projections change it by at most R||u||, while atomic depth>=Q gives a·z no greater than the atomic upper quantile. Thus r_Q<=2R/gamma_min.

The cap inequalities now give the exact formula

    T_Q(z)= (M/epsilon^N)
       inf_(y in int C_z) r_Q(z,y)^N/E_(C_z)(y).         (3)

For every finite threshold an interior minimizing mark exists by Section 2. In particular the infimum in (3) is attained. This is an inverse buffer threshold, not an inverse ordinary-energy depth estimate: r_Q retains ALL actual oblique mixed quantiles.

## 4. Sampled contacts, atomic plateaus, and a lattice-free region

Let ell be a positive sampled-concave array and use its roof on B. Fix Q to be the actual maximum buffered depth on the sampled fibers for this ell. Write I for its deepest bases, J={p in I:b_base(p)>Q}, and A=I outside J.

The exact projected REAL depth-Q region is

    {z in B:T_Q(z)<=ellhat(z)}.                          (4)

It is convex, directly because T_Q is convex and ellhat concave; its sampled trace is I. No assertion that all real bases in (4) are sampled is being made.

At a sampled base, the established whole-fiber capture and finite-tilt attainment lemmas give the following strict monotonicity: if the own maximum at l is positive and strictly below b_base(p), then reducing l strictly decreases that maximum. Proof by contradiction uses a maximizing mark for the reduced l, an attained old active cap there, and its proper OWN trace. Raising that cap threshold loses positive sampled own-fiber mass. Other sampled fibers can only lose mass. Supporting traces in those other fibers require no derivative.

This proves the complete sampled classification:

* If b_base(p)<Q, then T_Q(p)=infinity and p is not deepest.
* If b_base(p)>Q, then ell_p<=T_Q(p), with equality EXACTLY at p in J. At such a contact T_Q(p)=ell_p>0.
* If b_base(p)=Q, then p is deepest exactly when ell_p>=T_Q(p). Equality is allowed, but so is a strict atomic plateau ell_p>T_Q(p).

In particular the tempting universal sampled inequality ell<=T_Q is FALSE in the atomic stratum.

The convex set

    {z:b_base(z)>Q and T_Q(z)<ellhat(z)}                 (5)

contains no sampled base. The strict atomic superlevel is convex: since there are finitely many atomic traces, it equals a nonstrict superlevel at the next attainable mass above Q. Thus (5) is a precise projected lattice-free region. It need not be open on the boundary of its domain. On unsampled real bases the strict scalar monotonicity argument above is not imported: the source fiber there carries no atom of mixed base measure. Lattice-freeness uses the argument only at actual sampled points.

## 5. What the base-volume martingale can and cannot add

At the regular proper-source stationarity interface, the new unpenalized parameter theorem gives mu<=_cx nu, where mu is supported on J, nu is strictly positive at every sampled base, and every conditional row is ell-tight. Since T_Q=ell on J and the ell integrals agree, the additional convex test T_Q would give

    integral (T_Q-ell) dnu>=0,                          (6)

provided the target integral is finite. This is just a valid convex-order test, not equality or a support restriction. Often it is infinite, because positive target volume may lie outside (2). Neither a target-domain restriction nor contact equality follows from the martingale.

Here is an exact actual calibration of that obstruction. Use the certified three-interval family

    P={-1,0,1}, K_-=K_+=[-1,1], K_0=[-1,2],
    M=7, Sigma=43/84, ell=1, 0<epsilon<=10^(-4).

The audited all-slope formula gives the unique deepest mark

    y_epsilon=1/4+delta/2,
    Q=13/4+3delta/2,
    (1+t)delta^2-t delta-35t/4=0,
    t=43epsilon^2/1764.

This ell is the UNIQUE global parameter minimum over ALL positive normalized sampled-concave arrays, though not a joint body minimum. Indeed normalization and concavity force ell_0>=1, equality only at the constant array, and increasing ell_0 strictly increases the old middle optimum. Proper-minor quotas are strict and selected caps are regular.

For this weighted atomic base the depth is 5 at z=0 and exactly 2 at every other real z in [-1,1]. Since 2<Q<5, equation (2) gives

    dom T_Q={0},    T_Q(0)=1,    T_Q(z)=infinity (z!=0).

Nevertheless the exact normalized stationarity martingale is

    delta_0 --> (2 delta_-1+3 delta_0+2 delta_1)/7.

It sends 4/7 of its target mass OUTSIDE the entire threshold domain. This is a full-concave-parameter optimum with actual compatible fibers, not an arbitrary scalar marginal choice. It decisively prevents using the epigraph plus this martingale to assert that target volume lies on or even above finite contact fibers in its domain. The example is safe, Q/M>13/28, and makes no below-OC or joint body-minimum claim.

## 6. Scope and dependencies

The existing buffered-level theory already supplies joint concavity and cap quantiles; the new scalar formulation packages them into an exact closed convex threshold function, records its atomic domain, and distinguishes equality contacts from plateaus. The final calibration identifies a concrete obstruction to obtaining more support localization from parameter stationarity alone.

Dependencies used: the audited joint energy concavity/continuity; `candidate 5f79e6103cd27dac` for sampled base-gap cap attainment and properness; `candidate 14357e41460c996b` for the exact all-slope interval calculation; and `candidate cfe4a95984691190` for its all-concave optimum and volume martingale. No active-normal Slater condition, differentiable supporting-cap response, or uniform-fiber lift is assumed.
